brief: Credit markets remain open to hyperscalers: they priced ~$67bn of unsecured IG bonds (US+EUR) within 5 days since 9/30, so Morgan Stanley expects a quieter year-end. Post-midterms, combined 2027 capex forecasts stay unchanged at ~$1.66tr (+75% vs '26), but financing outcomes diverge along a widening quality divide: risk-reward improves for HQ hyperscalers (AMZN/GOOGL/META/MSFT) while data-center bonds and neoclouds see more spread volatility given execution and funding risk. Midterms push ~5GW of US IT capacity from 2028 to 2029 (Texas/Ohio projects not yet under construction), deepening the near-term power shortfall to 44GW through 2028, which reinforces the divide: largest companies can redirect investment, new construction faces more scrutiny. Leveraged finance stays subdued ($5bn in October). Data-center ABS spreads hit record wides on technical, not thematic, weakness; investors want amortization, which could tighten spreads if introduced. On single names: Oracle reaffirmed ~$20bn FY27 funding split evenly debt/equity, then priced $10bn bond plus $10bn equity after its Analyst Day; Amazon disclosed an $80bn supplier-financing facility; chip financing is accelerating ($103bn announced in October).
